record.Source: webster[Appendix B, printed p. 44 (PDF p. 49), item 99, DKS]

accepted.evidence: Turner connects cimṭā pincers and the pinch/cling verbs with *cimb. Platts explicitly gives cimṭī both pincers and ant and cross-refers the larger-ant cīṅṭā to cimṭā; this supplies the otherwise missing insect sense. The Nepal survey cimṭ-/cimt- forms are compared within this lexical family, without extending the analysis to the separate ciũṭ-/cuṭ- series.

record.Source: hugoniot-polster-ahmad-rajan2023easterngujari[Appendix B, PDF p. 58, printed p. 50, item 99, list UDH]

accepted.evidence: Turner’s kīṭa insect family includes Punjabi/Hindi/Gujarati kīṛī ant, beside kīṛā/kīṛo insect. Gujari kīṛo ant matches the same stem with a masculine ending and the documented narrower insect sense; this does not force a morphological analysis of the longer Bhili kiḍāvi forms.
